title: Integral chart logification on arbitrary schemes and strict first-order restriction
statement:
Let $T$ be any scheme [def-pc-scheme], not necessarily locally Noetherian, and let $P$ be a finitely generated integral commutative monoid: it has a finite generating set and embeds in its group completion. Let $\beta:P\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ be a monoid homomorphism, with multiplication on functions. A log structure here means a sheaf of commutative monoids $L$ on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site] with a map $\alpha:L\to(\mathcal O_T,\cdot)$ inducing an isomorphism $\alpha^{-1}(\mathcal O_T^\times)\simeq\mathcal O_T^\times$. It is integral if all geometric stalk monoids embed in their group completions, and fine if etale locally it has a chart by a finitely generated integral monoid.

For etale $U\to T$, put $E_U=\beta_U^{-1}(\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times)$. Sheafify the presheaf $U\mapsto P\oplus_{E_U}\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)^\times$ as a commutative-monoid sheaf [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification]; the pushout identifies $(pe,v)$ with $(p,\beta_U(e)v)$. Denote the resulting sheaf by $L_T(P,\beta)$, with structural map $[p,v]\mapsto\beta(p)v$. It is an integral fine log structure. At each geometric point $\bar t$, with $A=\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$ [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], it is canonically $P\oplus_{\beta^{-1}(A^\times)}A^\times$.

For every scheme map $a:S\to T$ and every log structure $K$ on $S$, homomorphisms of sheaves $a^{-1}L_T(P,\beta)\to K$ compatible with the structural maps and the ring map of $a$ correspond bijectively to monoid homomorphisms $v:P\to\Gamma(S,K)$ satisfying $\alpha_Kv=a^\sharp\beta$. Thus chart-compatible scheme maps have a unique compatible log map specified by their maps on $P$. Restriction of $L_T(P,\beta)$ to an etale $U$ is canonically $L_U(P,\beta_U)$.

Let $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be a first order thickening with ideal sheaf $\mathcal I$ [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], and give $T_0$ the associated log structure $L_{T_0}(P,\beta_0)$ for the reduced chart $\beta_0=j^\sharp\beta$. At corresponding geometric points the map $L_{T,\bar t}\to L_{T_0,\bar t}$ identifies the latter monoid with $L_{T,\bar t}\oplus_{A^\times}(A/\mathcal I_{\bar t})^\times$; in this sense the thickening is strict. Every fiber of this stalk map is a nonempty torsor under $1+\mathcal I_{\bar t}$: given any two lifts $m,m'$ of one log element, there is exactly one $v\in\mathcal I_{\bar t}$ with $m'=m(1+v)$. The same assertion is sheaf-local on the etale site, and multiplication on $1+\mathcal I$ corresponds to addition on $\mathcal I$ since $\mathcal I^2=0$.

source.place: Expose VI 1.1, printed p.69, associated-log and chart conventions referring to Kato (1988), section 1. Agent-formulated general chart-construction input for the infinitesimal tests in XVI Proposition 3.6.3, p.252; the general construction and strict-thickening assertion are not stated in ILO. WANTED: Kato (1988), Logarithmic structures of Fontaine--Illusie, section 1.

proof.text: Work in a common enlarged universe and on small skeletons as in [def-weil-size-convention], so the monoid sheafification theorem applies. Write $Q(U)=P\oplus_{E_U}\mathcal O(U)^\times$. This is concretely the quotient of $P\times\mathcal O(U)^\times$ by the displayed generating relations. Restriction sends $E_U$ into $E_V$ and preserves those relations, so defines a presheaf of commutative monoids. The maps $[p,u]\mapsto\beta_U(p)u$ also preserve the relations and restrictions. Units form a sheaf: glue the units and their inverses separately in the structure ring sheaf. By [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification], $L=Q^\#$ is a monoid sheaf whose underlying set sheaf is the set sheafification, and the structural map extends uniquely. Set $\iota(p)=\eta([p,1])$ and $j(u)=\eta([1,u])$; thus $\alpha j(u)=u$.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69, conventions; explicit construction using Sites Tag 00YR (section-sheaves-algebraic-structures).

proof.text: To verify the log axiom, let $l\in L(U)$ have unit image $a$. The local-representatives theorem [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local] writes $l$ locally as $\eta([p,u])$. There $\beta(p)=a/u$ is a unit, so $p\in E$ and $[p,u]=[1,\beta(p)u]=[1,a]$. Therefore $l=j(a)$ locally and globally. Conversely $\alpha j(a)=a$ proves that $j$ is injective and identifies precisely the inverse image of the units. This is the log axiom in the stated inline definition, without any Noetherian assumption.

source.place: VI 1.1, p.69, log convention; agent log-axiom argument using Sites Tag 00WK (lemma-sections-sheafification).

proof.text: Fix a geometric point and put $A=\mathcal O_{T,\bar t}$. By [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] this is the ring of germs of functions. The cofilteredness in [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-etale-neighbourhoods-cofiltered] implies that finitely many representatives and finitely many equalities of germs can be realized on one pointed refinement: a colimit equality is a finite chain of restriction relations, and a common source with equalized parallel maps realizes that chain. In particular a unit $a\in A^\times$ is represented by a unit on a neighbourhood: represent $a,a^{-1}$ together and refine until their product is $1$. Also $\beta_{\bar t}(e)$ is a unit exactly when $e\in E_U$ on some pointed neighbourhood, by the same inverse-and-equation argument.

source.place: Etale Cohomology Tag 03PQ (lemma-cofinal-etale), explicit finite germ equations.

proof.text: Let $E=\beta_{\bar t}^{-1}(A^\times)$. The colimit of $Q(U)$ maps to $P\oplus_E A^\times$ by $[p,u]\mapsto[p,u_{\bar t}]$. Conversely represent a unit $a\in A^\times$ on a pointed neighbourhood and send $(p,a)$ to the germ of $[p,u]$. Step 3 makes this independent of the representative. For each relation $(pe,a)\sim(p,\beta(e)a)$ in the target refine until $e\in E_U$; the relation then already holds in $Q(U)$. Thus this inverse descends through the generated congruence, and both composites fix represented pairs. Products are computed on common refinements, so these maps are monoid maps. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-sets-sheafification-geometric-stalk] and the underlying-set clause of [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] identify the colimit of $Q(U)$ with $L_{\bar t}$. This proves the stated canonical stalk formula, including its maps from $P$ and from $A^\times$.

source.place: Etale Cohomology Tag 03PT (lemma-stalk-exact) (2); explicit inverse on pairs.

proof.text: Apply [lem-per-integral-monoid-unit-pushout] to $P$, the submonoid $E$, the abelian group $A^\times$, and $f=\beta|_E$. Step 4 identifies its $M$ with $L_{\bar t}$; the embedding of $M$ in a group proves that every such stalk is integral. No injectivity of $\beta|_E$ is required. The global chart $\iota:P\to L(T)$ is the chart used to construct $L$, so it is a chart by the finitely generated integral monoid $P$ already on $T$. Consequently $L$ is fine in the stated definition.

source.place: VIII 3.1.2, p.98, integrality convention; agent application of the mixed pushout embedding.

proof.text:
Let $a:S\to T$ and $v:P\to K(S)$ have $\alpha_Kv=a^\sharp\beta$. On an etale $U\to T$ put $S_U=S\times_TU$. For $u\in\mathcal O(U)^\times$ let $a_U^\sharp u$ be its unit pullback. Define
$$Q(U)\longrightarrow K(S_U),\qquad [p,u]\longmapsto v(p)|_{S_U}\,j_K(a_U^\sharp u),$$
where $j_K$ is the inverse of the units isomorphism in the log axiom. For $e\in E_U$, $\alpha_K(v(e)|_{S_U})=a_U^\sharp\beta_U(e)$ is a unit, so $v(e)|_{S_U}=j_K(a_U^\sharp\beta_U(e))$. This proves that the displayed formula respects every generating relation. It is natural in $U$ and gives a monoid-presheaf map $Q\to a_*K$. Direct image is a sheaf (the inverse-image/direct-image adjunction of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]); hence [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] extends it uniquely to $L\to a_*K$.

source.place: VI 1.1 conventions and XVI 3.6.3 chart comparison, p.252; agent explicit construction of the map for arbitrary a.

proof.text: The set-sheaf adjunction and finite-product preservation in [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures](1) lift to monoids: inverse image sends the multiplication and identity diagrams to those for $a^{-1}L$, and an adjoint map preserves these operations exactly when its transpose does, by naturality of the adjunction. Transpose Step 6 to obtain $a^{-1}L\to K$. The structural compatibility is checked on each $[p,u]$, where both sides equal $(a^\sharp\beta(p))a^\sharp u$, and extends by sheafification uniqueness. Conversely a structurally compatible map, transposed to $L\to a_*K$, determines $v$ on $\iota(P)$. Its value on $j(u)$ is forced to be $j_K(a^\sharp u)$ by the log axiom of $K$. As $\eta([p,u])=\iota(p)j(u)$, its restriction to $Q$ is precisely Step 6. Sheafification uniqueness proves that these constructions are inverse. This gives the asserted bijection and uniqueness of a chart-specified log map.

source.place: VI 1.1 conventions; agent adjunction and inverse-map verification. Etale Cohomology Tag 03Q1 for inverse-image exactness.

proof.text: For etale $U\to T$, the small etale site of $U$ is the slice over $U$ of that of $T$: composition and cancellation are [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation], and coverings are the same jointly surjective families by [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The presheaf $Q_T$ restricted to this slice is exactly $Q_U$, with identical functions and relations. Restriction of $L_T$ is a sheaf; $Q_U\to L_T|_U$ is locally surjective and locally injective by [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-sections-local], since every refinement over an object of the slice still lies in the slice. By [lem-cbc-set-presheaf-sheafification-local-bijection] this identifies $L_T|_U$ with the set sheafification of $Q_U$. The underlying-set assertion of [lem-trf-commutative-monoid-sheafification] identifies this with $L_U$. The identification preserves multiplication, chart and structural map since it does so on all local pairs. This proves the claimed canonical restriction isomorphism.

source.place: Sites Tag 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification; Morphisms Tags 02GN and 02GW; explicit slice comparison.

proof.text: For $j:T_0\hookrightarrow T$, fix a corresponding geometric point. The affine pointed neighbourhoods compute the stalk by [lemma-weil-pbc-affine-neighbourhood-cofinal], so the ring $A$ is the strict-local ring colimit of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The quotient statement of [lem-trf-closed-immersion-strict-localization-cartesian] identifies the stalk ring of $T_0$ with $A/J$, where $J=\mathcal I_{\bar t}$. Indeed, on an affine chart with ideal $I$, the kernel is $IA$ by that node; germs of the ideal sheaf are exactly finite sums of elements of $I$ times germs of functions, so are $IA$. By [def-sbc-first-order-thickening], $I^2=0$ on affine charts and hence $J^2=0$. These results impose no Noetherian condition and keep the nilpotents of $T_0$.

source.place: Algebra Tag 05WS, lemma-quotient-strict-henselization; scheme strict-local form; More Morphisms Tag 04EX.

proof.text: For any commutative ring $A$ and square-zero ideal $J$, reduction $A^\times\to(A/J)^\times$ is surjective: lift $\bar a$ and $\bar a^{-1}$ to $a,b$, write $ab=1+c$ with $c\in J$, and use $a\,b(1-c)=1$. In particular an element of $A$ is a unit if and only if its reduction is. The kernel consists exactly of $1+c$, $c\in J$; each has inverse $1-c$. Moreover $(1+c)(1+d)=1+c+d$ since $cd=0$, and equality $1+c=1+d$ gives $c=d$. These calculations apply to Step 9 and show that the submonoid $E\subseteq P$ is identical before and after reduction.

source.place: Agent elementary square-zero calculation for the strict thickening assertion; VI 1.1 associated-log conventions.

proof.text:
The chart $P\to L_{T_0}(T_0)$ and Step 7 define the restriction log map. On stalks it sends $[p,u]\mapsto[p,\bar u]$, by its formula on charts and units. Step 4 on $T$ and on $T_0$, together with the equality of $E$ in Step 10, therefore gives $M=P\oplus_E A^\times$ and $M_0=P\oplus_E(A/J)^\times$. By [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-inverse-image-stalk-germ], the source of the sheaf pullback map has stalk $L_{T,\bar t}$, with these exact germs. The canonical identification
$$M\oplus_{A^\times}(A/J)^\times\simeq M_0$$
is obtained by $[[p,u],b]\mapsto[p,\bar u b]$ with inverse $[p,b]\mapsto[[p,1],b]$. Both formulas respect the pushout relations, and their composites fix each represented pair. This proves the stated strictness and its compatibility with the structural maps.

source.place: Etale Cohomology Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback (3); agent pushout identification.

proof.text: Every $[p,b]\in M_0$ lifts to $[p,u]\in M$, by the surjectivity on units in Step 10. If $m=[p,u]$ and $m'=[p',u']$ have the same image, apply the equality criterion of [lem-per-integral-monoid-unit-pushout] with $G=(A/J)^\times$. It gives $e,e'\in E$ with $pe'=p'e$ and $\bar u\,\overline{\beta(e)}=\bar u'\,\overline{\beta(e')}$. Put $c=\beta(e)$, $d=\beta(e')$, units in $A$. The defining relations give $m=[pe',u/d]$ and $m'=[p'e,u'/c]$, so $m'=mw$ for $w=u'd/(uc)$. The displayed reduced equality says $\bar w=1$, hence $w=1+v$ for a unique $v\in J$. The free unit action in the same cited node proves that no other $w$ can satisfy $m'=mw$, so this $v$ is unique. Thus each nonempty fiber is a torsor under $1+J$, and surjectivity shows that every fiber is nonempty.

source.place: Agent explicit fiber calculation using the mixed pushout equality criterion; VIII 3.1.2 integral-monoid convention.

proof.text:
Use [sbc-lem-thickening-etale-site] to identify the small etale sites by $U\mapsto U_0=U\times_TT_0$. In this identification put $N(U)=L_{T_0}(U_0)$, a sheaf on $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$. Its stalk at $\bar t$ is $M_0$ of Step 11: the equivalence of pointed neighbourhoods identifies the colimits and their germ maps. Every germ of $N$ has a lift in $L_T$ by Step 12. Representing the lift and its equality with a given local section on a pointed neighbourhood gives local surjectivity, hence such neighbourhoods cover. Consider the map of sheaves
$$(1+\mathcal I)\times L_T\longrightarrow L_T\times_NL_T,\qquad(w,m)\longmapsto(m,mw).$$
Its stalk maps are bijective by Step 12: finite tuples and their equations are represented on common pointed refinements as in Step 3. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-sets-etale-iso-on-geometric-stalks] to conclude this is an isomorphism. Thus any two lifts of the same local section differ by a unique local section of $1+\mathcal I$; the sheaf axiom glues the unique differences. Finally $(1+v)(1+w)=1+v+w$ on each object since $\mathcal I^2=0$, compatibly with restriction. This identifies $1+\mathcal I$ with the additive ideal sheaf. No surjectivity on global sections is asserted.

source.place: Etale Cohomology Tags 03SI (proposition-topological-invariance) and 03PU (theorem-exactness-stalks); agent local torsor calculation.
